purpose: Teach: 運河/レントゲン/怪物/満月/種族/蟹/椿/ほのぼの

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: 翔くん、お父さんと運河沿いをお散歩しましょうね
lines.en: Sho, let's go for a nice walk with Dad along the canal, shall we?
lines.style: Warm invitation, spoken from slightly above. Gentle certainty — not a question but an opening. Soft vocal weight on 'walk.' The mother settling her child into an idea.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: ママ、ぼく、明日レントゲン検査だから緊張するよ
lines.en: Mom, I'm nervous about my X-ray tomorrow.
lines.style: Quiet, specific worry. No dramatics. Small voice checking whether this concern is allowed. Slight pause before 'tomorrow' — he's been thinking about it. Eyes up toward her, gauging.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: 翔くん、絵本に出てくる怪物、可愛いわね
lines.en: Sho, the monsters in that picture book are rather cute, aren't they?
lines.style: Gentle redirection, half to herself. Observing her child's worry and trying to thread something hopeful past it. Warm, almost musing. Not ignoring what he said — honoring his worry by looking away first.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: ママ、ぼく、満月の夜にお祖父ちゃんとお月見したいよ
lines.en: Mom, I want to watch the full moon with Grandpa.
lines.style: Eager but tender — a small boy naming something he genuinely wants, not performing desire. Slight lift at 'full moon.' The dream is clear to him. Waiting to see if she'll help make it real.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: 翔くん、図書館で世界の種族について調べましょうね
lines.en: Sho, let's research the peoples of the world at the library, hmm?
lines.style: Patient suggestion, almost thinking aloud. An open door. No pressure — she's offering something bright because brightness matters right now. The vowels are soft, inviting.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: ママ、ぼく、お祖母ちゃんの蟹のお料理、大好きだよ
lines.en: Mom, I really love Grandma's crab dishes.
lines.style: Simple, genuine appreciation. Not performed — a small boy stating something true about his world. Warmth in the middle of the sentence. The kind of unprompted praise that makes a grandmother's whole week.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: 翔くん、お庭の椿、きれいに咲いてるわね
lines.en: Sho, the camellias in our garden are blooming beautifully, aren't they?
lines.style: Pleased observation, a small gift of noticing. She's bringing beauty into the space where worry lives. Light vocal weight. Not dismissing — anchoring to what's growing, what's alive, what's here.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: ママ、ぼく、お父さんとほのぼの過ごす時間が好き
lines.en: Mom, I like spending quiet, warm time with Dad.
lines.style: Tender confession, almost whispered. A small boy naming something he feels is safe. No urgency — just stating something true. Softness all the way through. The kind of vulnerability that only comes when a child feels held.
